fluid.purpose: Offer a smoother and more human contemporary reading while keeping every token-to-grapheme choice inspectable.

modern_palette.primary_reference: modern Basque orthography and system voice
modern_palette.rationale: The modern palette has five stable vowel letters and practical written distinctions for tap/trill and laminal/apical sibilants. It is selected for articulatory fit, not as evidence that Iberian sounded like Basque.

technical.purpose: Preserve a reproducible laboratory baseline for comparison, inspection and regression testing.

must_not_be_labelled: reconstrucción de cómo hablaban los íberos
prueba de parentesco entre ibérico y euskera

evidence_based_conventions.note: The five-vowel interpretation is broadly accepted; the exact ancient timbre remains unrecoverable.
Dental and velar dualities are rendered as voiced/voiceless. Their historical contrast may instead have involved fortis/lenis features.
These are conventional readable values, not measurements of ancient articulation.

explicit_hypotheses.note: The fluid Basque bridge uses z/s and the technical mode uses a laminal/apical contrast. Iberian historical values remain controversial.
Tap versus trill remains an audible project convention; the historical Iberian opposition is unknown.
The technical mode uses a syllabic nasal colour and the fluid bridge uses um only to keep the sign audible.

historical_boundaries.basque: A hypothetical relationship between Iberian and ancient or modern languages remains uncertain. The modern Basque palette is not used as a genealogical model.
historical_boundaries.celtic: Celtiberian was a different Indo-European language and is not used as a pronunciation model for Iberian.
historical_boundaries.arabic: Arabic belongs to a later historical horizon in the peninsula and is not used as a pronunciation model for Iberian.
historical_boundaries.prosody: No Iberian stress or intonation system can currently be recovered well enough to drive speech synthesis.
